title: Building and Scaling an AI Agent Swarm of low latency real time voice bots: Damien Murphy
talk_summary: A Deepgram engineer demos a low-latency voice-agent API and discusses scaling voice bots with function calling, endpointing, and multi-agent routing. The transferable lessons are mostly orchestration patterns: narrow composable agents, lean prompts with dynamic tool-fetched context, non-blocking long-running tool calls, cheap-model routing, output-side validation, and tracing.

takeaways.what_they_do: They avoid one mega-agent/system prompt and instead build narrow agents for specific tasks, then route/compose them into larger flows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't want to create an agent that does everything ... create an agent that's capable at a particular task and then build them together

takeaways.technique: Lean static prompts, fetch dynamic context via tools
takeaways.what_they_do: They keep large dynamic data like menus out of the system prompt and expose it as a function call so the model fetches only what it needs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you could remove that menu from there and add it as a function call
takeaways.numbers: Speaker cites ~900ms first-token latency for GPT-4o and ~30 tokens/sec for most LLMs.

takeaways.technique: Non-blocking long-running tool calls with callback
takeaways.what_they_do: For slow work, the LLM kicks off a job and returns immediately; a backend webhook later prompts the LLM when the job completes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the llm would just say hey go do this long running task instantly return

takeaways.what_they_do: They recommend using the smallest/cheapest model that can achieve the use case, while noting newer models are needed for reliable function calling.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use the smallest cheapest model you can to achieve the use case

takeaways.what_they_do: They accept prompt injection is hard to block on input, so they inspect assistant output/conversation text and block invalid or disallowed actions before they take effect.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're not going to be able to stop it on the way in but on the way out you could be like hey

takeaways.technique: Trace every agent/tool step for debugging
takeaways.what_they_do: They point to agent-ops tooling that records the LLM flow so teams can debug what happened across steps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: temporal debugging so you can actually debug what was happening throughout the llm flow
